title: New Cardamom Variety - Njallani

details.full_description:
late sebastian  josephji had developed njallani variety of cardamom from idukki, kerala. he observed variations in the clones and in the shape of berries. from this he selected 4 plants and kept hives in the middle of these plants. the clones with more berries and bigger size were elected. the selected four clones produced 148 berries. these capsules were of double in size than common mysore variety. he called his selection njallani after the ancestral name. sebastian began to multiply this selected variety by the clonal propagation. he selected clonal propagation by vegetative method instead of planting seedlings because seedlings usually takes up 2-3 years for fruiting. by clonal propagation method the farmers can obtain the yield from 2nd year of planting.

salient features of the variety:
• yield: 1000 kg / hectare
• berries of this variety is three times larger than the local variety
• clonal propagation by vegetative method helps farmer to get yield in the 2 year
• plant height: 8 - 10 meter
• days to flowering: 15 months & days to maturity: 110 days
• number of capsules per panicle: 120-160 capsules/panicle
• number of seeds per capsule: 25-32 seeds / capsule

title: Traditional variety of Tinda (round guard) preserved by Kir community

details.full_description:
the fruits of traditional variety of tinda (round gourd) are tender, delicious in taste. fruits are flat round in shape and weighs around 100 to 200 g at the time of harvesting. prolific vines spread up to 40 to 50 inches long, 10-12 vines/plant having hairs structures on the stems, leaves and fruits, while, other commercial varieties do not have hairs on fruits.  it has to be sown within the month of jan to april. it is purely a desi/local variety having large number of hairs; fruits are greenish white in colour and have high market value as compared to other varieties. flowering begins at 30 to 35 days after sowing and first picking can be done at 15 to 20 days after flowering. 

this variety produces 200 to 250 q fruits per hectare and is popular in neighboring villages too. the seed merchant purchase seeds of this variety directly from farmers for selling it to other places of rajasthan and other stated as well. fruits of this variety are famous as “sahapur tinda” due to large-scale cultivation in this area. the variety is superior in terms of yield and quality as compared to other commercially cultivated varieties. many farmers of this village have started cultivation of this variety for seed production only. farmers in this village have produced about 300 q seeds of this variety every year. it is resistant to insect-pest & diseases but susceptible to blight disease. the variety is most suitable in irrigated area and requires 8-10 irrigations throughout the season.

title: Root Wilt Disease (RWD) Resistant Black Pepper Variety

details.full_description: mr. ravishanka has developed a root wilt disease resistant black pepper variety. crop: black pepper ( piper nigrum l.) salient features: resistance to root wilt disease, early flowering, increased no. of berries per spike. genesis: mr. ravishanka found hippali, a wild long pepper variety had roots hard enough to resist root wilt. root wilt is a severe problem in pepper and leads to severe loss in production. by using hippali variety as rootstock, which is resistant to wilt and not detrimental to the stock, he developed a wilt resistant pepper variety through grafting technique. he grafted hippali with local cultivars viz. panniyur in the year 2001-02. the variety developed was found to be resistant to wilt disease and could withstand drought conditions. cropping season: rabi
details.Salient features: Resistance to root wilt disease, Early flowering, Increased no. of berries per spike.

By using Hippali variety as rootstock, which is resistant to wilt and not detrimental to the stock, he developed a wilt resistant pepper variety through grafting technique. He grafted Hippali with local cultivars viz. Panniyur in the year 2001-02. The variety developed was found to be resistant to wilt disease and could withstand drought conditions.

title: Controlling of Smut in Sorghum

details.full_description: mr bacchubhai lakshmanbhai rathod from gujarat has developed the herbal preparation for control of smut in sorghum targeted pest: fungi ( smut disease) targeted crop: sorghum bicolor . (l.) moench ingredients: aristolochia bracteolata lam., clerodendrum volubile p.beauv. methodology: he crushes the leaves of both plants to prepare an extract from it. then mix the extract with water to prepare a formulation. use this formulation for seed treatment and provides good control against smut disease in sorghum. suggested reading(s): kavitha, d., & nirmaladevi, r. (2009). assessment of aristolochia bracteolata leaf extracts for its biotherapeutic potential. african journal of biotechnology , 8 (17), 4242-4244.

title:
Multi Utility Herbal Formulation:
Kamaal 505

details.full_description:
shri ishwar singh (61 years) hails from kaithal district of haryana. he has completed iti and after that he was involved in agriculture. shri ishwar singh has developed “multiutility formulation” based on several plant ingredients. it acts as
growth promoter, fungicide, and termiticide. due to its high organic carbon content, it improves soil fertility, increases water intake and enhances water-holding capacity of the soil. it is a good source of zinc (27.35 mg/kg), copper (5.11 mg/kg)
and manganese (173.60 mg/kg) as well as organic carbon (45.7%) and is free harmful elements like arsenic. the formulation improves soil micro and macro fauna, reduces cost of cultivation and enhances water holding capacity of saline
and compact soils.

title: Organic Pest Control Measures

details.full_description:
mariamma thomas from malappuram, kerala has  invented this organic pest controlmethod. he prepares five to six feet pandals for creepy (cucurbitaceous) vegetables. this makes easy for the creepers to grow and for us to pick the vegetables. she suggests fuming instead of insecticide sprays for cucurbitaceous vegetables like bitter gourds (karela) and kuluru.
she takes 1 kg dried cow dung in an earthen pot and mixes  it with 15 gms of tobacco. then she fumes this mixture by keeping the earthen pot below the vegetable canopy. the smoke is enough to kill the harmful pests. the procedure is beaing repeated every week. for treatment of insects and pests affecting grams (choli), grind 25 gms of tobacco dilute with water and keep overnight. in the morning, mix it with a little quantity of coconut oil and soap solution and sprinkle on the leaves of choli.

title: Herbal Pesticide for Fruit and Vegetable Crops

details.full_description:
mr ganesh dutt sharma from  himachal pradesh has developed the herbal preparation for control of pest in fruit and vegetable targeted pest: white grub, cutworm, heliothis targeted crop: fruit and vegetable ingredients: colebrookea oppositifolia sm., ageratum conyzoides l., persicaria hydropiper (l.) delarbre, spermadictyon suaveolens roxb., ipomoea carnea subsp. fistulosa (mart.
ex choisy) d.f.austin, cow urine methodology: he takes 2 kg of all 5 plants (hareraphul - colebrookea oppositifolia , ujadu - ageratum conyzoides , pirpiri - polygonum hydropiper , nilikathi - spermadictyon suaveolens , besharmbuti - ipomoea fistulosa ) and mix it with 10 l cow urine and keep in a vessel for 15 days. after 15 days, filter the mixture and add 50 ml essential oil of hareraphul - colebrookea oppositifolia . for spraying in 1 bigha take 200 ml of the mixture and mix it with 10 l water properly. spray it on vegetable and fruits crop in the evening to prevent evaporation. use the herbal formulation to control gahali (white grub), fundiya, hara kida (cutworm), kala kida (heliothis) in vegetable and fruits crop and store it for one year at a dose of 200 ml stock in 10 l of water. suggested reading(s): brari, j., kumar, v., & thakur, d. r. title: Control of Brown Plant Hopper in Paddy

details.full_description: shri basav raj santeshivara  has developed a methodology at his native place hassan, karnataka for controlling brown hopper in paddy. during the day time, he holds a stick parallel to the ground and walks slowly commoving the top of the paddy plants from one end of the field to the other. this disturbs the hoppers settled on the top, and as he walks forward with the stick, the hoppers jump from plant to plant and finally to the fire set or pesticide (preferably herbal ones) sprayed at the end of the field. the hoppers will be attracted by the light if a person walks in the night with a torch in hands. the hoppers will simply follow the light for a fair distance. he has also developed several organic farming methods like effective composting through coir pit and gober gas slurry.

title: Cultivation of Cotton in Water Stress condition

details.full_description: mr. harbhajan singh from fatehabad, haryana has developed cotton cultivation in water stress condition targeted crop: cotton ingredients: sowing pattern methodology: he sows cotton seeds on the ridges of the water channel, which is two feet in width and separates each channel by the distance of six feet. apply water in the channel, the six feet space is left as such. this reduces the water requirement and controls the weeds. this method of sowing controls wilt and other ball diseases, yield remains equal to normal sowing pattern.

title: Bio-control Measure Against Hoppers

details.full_description: mr. b.s.dinesh from shimoga, karnataka has developed herbal practice for bio-control measure against hoppers targeted pest: paddy hoppers targeted crop: paddy ( oryza sativa l.) ingredients: lasiosiphon glaucus fresen. methodology: he uses the decoction of leaves of a local herb mukkadaka ( lasiosiphon eriocephalus decne.). prepare a decoction of a kilogram of mukkadaka leaves in 10 litres of water, filter and dilute it in 1:10 ratio. spray it twice, once during nursery stage and then after transplanting paddy. the decoction is also effective against crabs, which otherwise cut the plants at a very tender stage. suggested reading(s): gupta, a., goldie, o., annika, d., & sharon, m. (2012). bactericidal effect of crude extracts of an endangered plant: lasiosiphon eriocephalus decne. j. microbiol. biotech. res , 2 (6), 866-870.

(kuwar-patha) + neem oil 500 ml + tobacco snuff decoction 500ml should be added in 20 lits. of water and boiled for 3 to 4 hours. after that, when the volume of water would decrease to about 5 lits. it should be allowed to become cold and sieved properly. this should be sprayed on cotton, lady's finger (bhindi) etc.                                               2. in this method calotropis sps. are to be grown around the field of crop plants by rajnikantbhai patel (from sabarkantha, gujarat) in which the ladybird beetle would take shelter. the calotropis leaves should be then spread in the field so that the ladybird beetles could easily feed on the sucking pests, as it is a predator of sucking pests. thus, the sucking pests could be controlled.                                               3. rajnikantbhai patel from sabarkantha, gujarat has suggested some plant, plant parts and extracts to manage certain pests are mentioned below.
• the latex of euphorbia nerifolia can be used to control wilt, rotting and termites in various crop plants like pomegranate, castor, wheat, legumes etc.
• the juice of leaves of hautana camara, can be used to control white flies. due to control of these flies, wilt in cotton can be controlled, since white flies act as a vector of wilt. in this process only the apical leaves are utilized.
• the extract of jatropha can be used for the control of sucking pests.
• salvadora loeoides can be used for the control of powdery mildew.
• nicotiana tobacum powder is used to control prodenia.

title: Technique to control Rice Bug attack on Paddy

details.full_description:
shri k d kharkongor (from shilong, meghalaya) has developed a new technique for trapping rice bugs by blending traditional knowledge of ‘khasis’ and ‘heli catch technique’ developed by a private company. he has thus come up with the idea of using baffle traps with dead crabs to attract rice bugs instead of ‘pheromone lures’. it needs minimum of four traps in one field and maximum of seven to eight traps in a field with heavy infestation.
the innovator also experimented by using intestines of chicken/goat and other materials emanating similar foul smell, in place of crab and got good success.

title: Protection of seedlings of Chilli plant from Gavala - Insect

details.full_description: kapuriben sardarsingh lives at dahod, gujarat developed a technique to protect the seedlings of chillies from gavala (an insect in gujarati). she uses the branches of "kada" plant are spread over on the seedlings. due to the bitterness of the leaves of kada, the gavala runs off from that place. it also controls the moisture level of seedlings.

title: Controlling of Heliothis in Lady's Finger

details.full_description: mr kantibhai vankar  from gujarat had developed the herbal preparation for control of heliothis in okra targeted pest: heliothis targeted crop: okra ingredients: foeniculum vulgare mill. methodology: he uses 1 kg fenugreek powder mix it with 2-litre normal water and he keeps this liquid aside for 24 hours. spray this mixture on the standing crop of lady's finger. suggested reading(s): kim, d. h., & ahn, y. j. (2001). contact and fumigant activities of constituents of foeniculum vulgare fruit against three coleopteran stored?product insects. pest management science: formerly pesticide science , 57 (3), 301-306.

title: Controlling of Leaf Curl in Chilli Crops

details.full_description: mr rameshbhai virsinhbhai bariya from gujarat has developed the herbal preparation for control of leaf curl in chilli crops targeted pest: thrips (leaf curl) targeted crop: chilli ingredients: commiphora wightii (arn.) bhandari, zea mays l., sugar methodology: in the practice bark of mukul, maize flour and sugar is used. due to leaf curl, the growth of the plant, flowering in plants is affected a lot and it declines. so the vapour of the mixture made from the above components is given to managing leaf curl in plants. suggested reading(s): montes-molina, j. a., luna-guido, m. l., espinoza-paz, n., govaerts, b., gutierrez-miceli, f. a., & dendooven, y. l. title: Practice to Prevent Discoloration in Okra & Chilli

details.full_description: mr v k jayaveeran from tamil nadu has developed the herbal preparation for discoloration in okra & chilli targeted pest: discoloration targeted crop: okra & chilli ingredients: prosopis juliflora (sw.) dc. methodology: juice is extracted from the leaves of prosopis juliflora and diluted with water then sprayed in chilli (capsicum spp) fields two months after planting. for spraying one acre, three-litre of leaf extract is required. when 'bhendi' (okra) pods are discoloured (light yellow or white) the same extract is sprayed on the field. suggested reading(s): oliveira, a. s., pereira, r. a., lima, l. m., morais, a. h., melo, f. r., franco, o. l., ... & sales, m. p. title: Controlling of Leaf Curl in Chilli and Brinjal crops

details.full_description: ms rupiben pratapbhai macchar from gujarat had developed the herbal preparation for control of leaf curl in chilli and brinjal crops targeted pest: thrips (leaf curl) targeted crop: chilli, brinjal ingredients: goat milk methodology: she uses the milk of a goat. with the help of the broom sprayer, the goat’s milk is sprayed on the plants. this practice is found to be very effective.

title: Tapioca water as Insecticide

details.full_description: mr. jospeh from idukki, kerala found an innovative method for preventing the scales in pepper. tapioca is usually dried after being put in hot water for some time, this water is sticky in nature and can be poured on the affected plants and it would stay on the leaves of the pepper killing the scale germs.

title: Controlling of Pests in Paddy and Vegetables

details.full_description: mr moirngthem ibobi meitei from manipur has developed the herbal preparation for controlling pest in paddy & vegetables targeted pest: paddy & vegetable pests targeted crop: paddy, vegetables ingredients: ageratum conyzoides l. methodology: for this preparation take the fresh jangli pudina ( ageratum conyzoides ) plant and shade dry them. crush the plant into powder. take 500g of powder of ageratum conyzoides mix it with 2 litres of water and 50g of soda soap. keep the solution for 1-2 hours to get final preparation for foliar application. suggested reading(s): ming, l. c. (1999). ageratum conyzoides : a tropical source of medicinal and agricultural products. perspectives on new crops and new uses , (alexandria), 469-473.

title: Controlling of Pest in Paddy Crop

details.full_description: ms gangiya devi from jharkhand has developed the herbal preparation for controlling of pest in paddy targeted pest: paddy pests targeted crop: paddy ingredients: adina cordifolia (roxb.) brandis methodology: she is using fresh stalks of adina cordifolia with leaves for controlling insects in paddy field. the insects will move away from the field where stalks are used. the leaves of adina cordifolia has been reported for having excellent antifeedant and insecticidal activities against agriculture pests.

title: Herbal Formulations for insect-pest control in vegetable and paddy crops

details.full_description: late smt. janki devi was an innovative farmer in his locality of west champaran, bihar and famous as a pesticide lady. she happily shared her knowledge to control insects in agriculture crops by using herbal practices. the leaves of murraya and whole plant of parthenium are taken in equal quantity (100gm each) and crush them by mixing of 500ml water. squeeze the juice with the help of muslin cloth to get final formulation for foliar application. the foliar application should be done at evening time for effective pest control. the solution can be stored for about six months. both the plants were tested for their insecticidal activities against crops insects and mosquitoes and found to be very effective for insects control in paddy and vegetable crops.

title: Herbal preparation for controlling of paddy pests

details.full_description: smt. devkumari (50 years old) is a house wife and has primary education. she lives in a village gada of sitamarhi district of bihar. she shared her knowledge about pest control in paddy field.  in this practice, the leaves of banana are chopped in very small pieces and spreading in whole field of paddy. it can be used twice and trice in a cropping season for effectively pests control. the fermented for 24 hours and fresh juice were tested against termite attack on gunny bags, coconut frond, wooden frame work and wooden pillars at different concentration 5%, 10%, 25%, 50% and 100%. there was no termite attack for 50 days on experimental materials treated with 50 and 100% concentrated of fermented juice. it was also tested against spodoptera litura in laboratory condition and mortality was found 20 percent over positive control.

title: Controlling of Leaf Folder in Paddy Crop

details.full_description: mr ratilal shamaldas patel from gujarat has developed the herbal preparation for controlling of leaf folder in paddy targeted pest: paddy pests targeted crop: paddy ingredients: ricinus communis l., cow dung methodology: he prepares a mixture of 1 litre of castor ( ricinus communis ) oil and 20 kg ashes of cow dung for pest and disease control. this mixture is broadcasted during the evening time in paddy crop. the mixture shows its effect within two to three days. the mixture of 30 kilograms is sufficient for one acre. suggested reading(s): rani, p. u., & ravibabu, m. v. (2011). allelochemicals in castor ( ricinus communis l.) plants and their impact on pest larval feeding as anti-herbivore defensive. allelopathy journal , 27 (2).

title: Herbal Preparation for Controlling Grasshopper in Paddy Crop

details.full_description: mr. mulchand thakur from jharkhand had developed a herbal preparation for controlling grasshopper in paddy targeted pest: grasshopper. targeted crop: paddy. ingredients: 500 g each of, bark of holarrhena pubescens wall. ex g.don, leaves of pongamia pinnata (l.) panigrahi, leaves of vitex negundo l., leaves of azadirachta indica a.juss., leaves of chloroxylon swietenia dc., 3 l cow urine. methodology: take fresh leaves and bark of the plants and crush them together properly. add cow urine to prepare a solution and keep for 15 days. after 15 days mix properly and sieve the infusion with the help of muslin cloth. 100 ml of prepared infusion is used per 10 l water, and sprayed over the infested paddy crop. all ingredients used in this practice are well known for their insecticidal activities. dose: 100 ml in 10 l of water for spraying.

title: Controlling of Pests in Vegetable Crops

details.full_description: ms krishnavati devi from bihar had developed the herbal preparation for controlling pest in paddy targeted pest: vegetable pests targeted crop: vegetable ingredients: croton bonplandianus baill. methodology: for the preparation of spray fluid take one kilogram of croton bonplandianum (roots and leaf) plant with a two-litre of water. it is crushed and kept for four days in an earthen pot. after four days, it is filtered and add two-litre of water in one litre of prepared solution for spraying over the vegetable crops. it is effective against sucking pests in vegetable crops. the stock solution of 3 litres is sufficient for a one-acre area of the field. suggested reading(s): jeeshna, m. v., mallikadevi, t., & paulsamy, s. (2010). screening of the weed plant species, croton bonplandianum baill. for larvicidal activity of aedes aegypti . journal of biopesticides , 3 (1), 192.

title: Controlling of Pest in Okra

details.full_description: mr bhikhabhai kalubhai solanki from gujarat had developed the herbal preparation for pest control in okra crop targeted pest: okra pests targeted crop: okra ingredients: clerodendrum phlomidis l.f. , cow urine methodology: for this five hundred gram fresh leaves of bhramarmal/ bhargi (clerodendrum) are taken, chopped and 500 ml water is added. the above material is finely ground to extract the juice. the extract solution obtained from above is squeezed and filtered with the help of muslin cloth. one hundred and fifty ml of stock solution is taken and an equal amount of cow urine is added at the time of spraying. dilute the above mixture in 15 liters of water and then spray it on the crops at a dose of 300ml/15 litre of water. suggested reading(s): muthu, c., reegan, a. d., kingsley, s., & ignacimuthu, s. (2012). larvicidal activity of pectolinaringenin from clerodendrum phlomidis l. against culex quinquefasciatus say and aedes aegypti l.(diptera: culicidae). parasitology research , 111 (3), 1059-1065.

title: Controlling Pests in Vegetable and Paddy Crops

details.full_description: mr badri mahato from bihar has developed the herbal preparation for pest control in paddy and vegetable crops targeted pest: sucking pests targeted crop: paddy and vegetable ingredients: mikania micrantha kunth, sphaeranthus africanus l. methodology: 1. chop one kg of the aerial portion of the mikania micrantha into small pieces and boil it into 2.0 litres of water. when the plant goes to melt, remove it from fire and filter the extract through a muslin cloth. apply foliar spray on the affected crops. for best result, three sprays should be done at 10 days interval. for the foliar application, 1.5 litre of stock solution is sufficient in for one acre.  2. cut leaves of one kilogram of guder/bhuin/kadamba ( sphaeranthus indicus ) into small pieces and soak it in 3-litre water for a day. strain the liquid portion and use it for foliar application at a dose of 1.5 litres of stock solution is sufficient in for one acre. suggested reading(s): komalamisra, n., trongtokit, y., rongsriyam, y., & apiwathnasorn, c. (2005). screening for larvicidal activity in some thai plants against four mosquito vector species. southeast asian journal of tropical medicine and public health , 36 (6), 1412.

title: Controlling Leaf Folder in Paddy and Fruit Borer in Vegetable Crops

details.full_description: mr rajesh mishra from bihar had developed the herbal preparation for controlling borer in vegetable crops & leaf folder in paddy targeted pest: borer, leaf folder targeted crop: vegetable, paddy ingredients: azadirachta indica a.juss. , erythrina abyssinica lam. methodology: for this two hundred and fifty gram fresh leaves each of azadirachta indica and erythrina suberosa (paldhua) are crushed separately by adding 100 ml of water. the crushed plant sample is squeezed and filtered in a vessel and mixed with each other. the filtrate preparation is kept in sunlight for 3 hrs. one litre of the solution is sufficient for one acre of crop. a litre of stock solution can be obtained from 3 kilograms each of the two plants mentioned above. innovator uses the formulation to control pests in vegetable crops and leaf folder in paddy. suggested reading(s): ahmed, s., & grainge, m. title: New Method in Vanilla Cultivation

details.full_description: mr george mathew from kottayam, kerala has developed a new method for the cultivation of vanilla targeted crop: vanilla ( vanilla planifolia andrews) methodology: a one-metre long stem of vanilla is planted initially. after six months, it starts sprouting from where it was bent below the node. after nine months, it starts flowering between the sprout and the point of cut. after one year, the second sprout starts at the point of the initial bend. the stem is cut one metre away from the point of the second sprout. it starts flowering and fruiting in bunches from all the stems that have got cut at their end. tie these bunches to the stem to make them grow straight. sprouting took place at every bending point of the stem. this methodology helps the farmer in getting double yield and farmer can decide where to grow bunches and where to grow fruits.

title: Use of buttermilk as  coagulant for rubber latex

details.full_description: mr shankara patali had developed the technique -  use of buttermilk as  coagulant for rubber latex targeted crop: rubber ingredients: buttermilk methodology: to prepare rubber sheets, on the first day 250 ml of water and around 150-250 ml of sour buttermilk is added to two litres of filtered latex in the tray and is churned well till the froth is formed. the froth formed is then removed immediately. the same procedure is followed for the first four days. on the fifth day the sheet is passed through the rollers so that the sheet becomes thin and extra water is drained out of it. this water is collected and kept aside for three days so that it gets fermented. this step should be followed regularly. then on the fifth day, the use of buttermilk is discontinued and instead of it the fermented liquid is used. the amount of this liquid, to be used varies from season to season i.e. 300-500 ml in winter and 150-250 ml in summer. this is done because the density and consistency of latex varies according to climatic conditions and time period. while processing grade sheets, the drained fermented water should be thoroughly strained and used. if the process requires making sheets on the same day, fermented water should be added twice more than the normal quantity and less than 250ml or no water must be added. if the latex is being processed once in two days, it is advisable to use the drained water as such without allowing it to ferment- during winters (250-300ml) and during summers (150-200ml) on the same day. the quantity of buttermilk to be used will be some extent depends on the seasonal variations, temperature, and the latex quality. the older the buttermilk or fermented liquid the greater the effect and lesser quantity needs to be used.

title: Perrenial brinjal varieties (Two varieties)

details.full_description: shri p. r .krishna prasad is a farmer from karnataka. he had developed a perennial brinjal varieties (two varieties) crop: solanum melongena l. (brinjal) salient features: both the brinjal varieties are not only high yielding but also have medicinal properties. their fruits are beneficial to diabetic patients. they are resistant to diseases, drought tolerant, cost effective and highly remunerative. a perennial brinjal tree which is not fully high yielding, but also resistant to diseases and cost effective and high remunerative, continuous fruit bearer throughout the year was developed. 1) tall tree type (prk -1 or karthik raksha) it has potential to grow to a height of about 15-20 ft. at present it is 10 tall bearing heavily and continuously which is 1 year and 10 months old. the yield potential may range from 25,000 to 60,000 kg/ acre/year - 900 to 1200 plants/ acre. it is resistant to bacterial, fungal wilts and nematodes. 2) bushy type (prk - 2 or anugocori) it has potential to grow to a height of 6 to 8 feet, with a life span of 6 to 8 years. the yield ranges from 10,000 to 50,000 kgs/acre/year - 2000 plants/acre. advantages : yielding potential is several times higher than the present varieties. it provides fuel for the farmers. it is resistant to major diseases and tolerant to drought. easily cultivated & cheap to maintain. the fruits are more beneficial to diabetic patients. it improves human life standard and is environmentally friendly.it can also be grown on roadsides, restaurants, as an ornamental plant, etc. genesis: prk-1 or karthik raksha which is tall tree type and prk -2 or anugowri which is bushy type. both the varieties could be grown with little investment and minimum maintenance and they could remain productive throughout the year. this tree is developed through grafting and keeps bearing throughout the year for many years. using grafting 2 varieties have been developed. cropping season: rabi
details.Salient features: Both the brinjal varieties are not only high yielding but also have medicinal properties. Their fruits are beneficial to diabetic patients. A perennial brinjal tree which is not fully high yielding, but also resistant to diseases and cost effective and high remunerative, continuous fruit bearer throughout the year was developed. 1) Tall Tree Type (PRK -1 or Karthik Raksha) It has potential to grow to a height of about 15-20 ft. At present it is 10 tall bearing heavily and continuously which is 1 year and 10 months old. The yield potential may range from 25,000 to 60,000 kg/ Acre/year - 900 to 1200 plants/ Acre. It is resistant to bacterial, fungal wilts and nematodes. 2) Bushy Type (PRK - 2 or Anugocori) It has potential to grow to a height of 6 to 8 feet, with a life span of 6 to 8 years. The yield ranges from 10,000 to 50,000 kgs/Acre/year - 2000 plants/acre. Advantages : Yielding potential is several times higher than the present varieties. It provides fuel for the farmers. It is resistant to major diseases and tolerant to drought. Easily cultivated & cheap to maintain. The fruits are more beneficial to diabetic patients. It improves human life standard and is environmentally friendly.It can also be grown on roadsides, restaurants, as an ornamental plant, etc.
details.Genesis: PRK-1 or Karthik raksha which is tall tree type and PRK -2 or Anugowri which is bushy type. Both the varieties could be grown with little investment and minimum maintenance and they could remain productive throughout the year. This tree is developed through grafting and keeps bearing throughout the year for many years. Using grafting 2 varieties have been developed.

mr. bhikhubhai g patel has developed the herbal practice to control termite in mango. targeted pest: termite targeted crop: mango ( mangifera indica l.) ingredients: seeds of brilliant gardenia ( gardenia resinifera roth), ocher. methodology: he uses about 150 to 250 g seeds of brilliant gardenia and 100 g ocher. he dries and grinds them together so as to make a powder. then he adds about 1 l of water to form a solution. he smears the solution on the trunk of mango tree up to 2 to 3 feet height from ground level. this has a repellent action resulting in termite control. suggested reading(s): raghavendra, h., shilpa,
m., pushpavathi, d., petkar, t., & siddiqha, a. antimicrobial, antiradical
and insecticidal activity of gardenia gummifera l.f.(rubiaceae). international journal of pharmacy and pharmaceutical
sciences , 9 (10), 265-272.
details.Ingredients: Seeds of Brilliant gardenia (Gardenia resiniferaRoth), Ocher.
details.Methodology: He uses about 150 to 250 g seeds of Brilliant gardenia and 100 g ocher. He dries and grinds them together so as to make a powder. Then he adds about 1 L of water to form a solution. He smears the solution on the trunk of mango tree up to 2 to 3 feet height from ground level. This has a repellent action resulting in termite control.

title: Practice to Control White Grub in Groundnut Crop

details.full_description: mr. kesharam bhagvanram mehra has developed the herbal practice to control white grub in groundnut crop targeted pest: white grub targeted crop: groundnut ingredients: calcium oxide methodology: he buys quick lime and exposes it to air for 2 to 3 hours, which makes it soft and granular. he then spreads (40 to 50 kg/hectare) the prepared quick lime has to be on the field before the onset of monsoon. thereafter, he ploughs the field once to mix the quick lime thoroughly in the soil.

title: Practice to Store Wheat Grain

details.full_description: mr. dudabhai arjanbhai pandav has developed a herbal practice to store wheat grain. targeted crop: wheat ingredients: straw of wheat ( triticum aestivum l.). methodology: he uses wheat straw for storing wheat grains. in a room of 10 feet x 10 feet area, he makes layer of wheat straw of about 2 feet height and then pressed material and stored wheat grains on it. the grains are safe from insect pests for 1 year period. 2000 to 3000 kg wheat grains can be stored in this space.

title: Storage Practice of Onion

details.full_description: mr. hakabhai samlabhai sarviya has developed the herbal practice for storage of onion. targeted crop: onion ( allium cepa l.). ingredients: cotton ( gossypium l.), and  indian elm ( holarrhena pubescens wall. ex g.don.). methodology: he uses a basket made up from the stalks of cotton and indian elm. he places the indian elm at the bottom of the basket before placing the onion, by which the process of turning is not advocated. then he places the onion bulbs in to the basket for storage. the onion can be stored in this process for 1 year. suggested reading(s): thappa, r. k., tikku, k., saxena, b. p., vaid, r. m., & bhutani, k. k. title: Practice to Increase Yield by Proper Crop Rotation

americanus(L.) Morrone).

title: Grafting in Bitter Gourd

details.full_description: ms. kastarben bhagwanbhai gajera has developed the herbal practice for grafting in bitter gourd. targeted crop: bitter gourd ( momordica charantia l.). ingredients: ridge gourd ( luffa acutangula (l.) roxb.). methodology: at the time of flowering of ridge gourd, she cuts the vine at 1 feet from the base and grafts the branches of bitter gourd on it by wedge graft method. after grafting she covers the grafted part with wet soil and ties a cloth over it and keeps for 15 to 20 days. this helps in joining of two plants. the fruit of such grafted plant is long bitter gourd. again she sows the seeds from this grafted plant to produce long fruits of bitter gourd which is less bitter in taste. suggested reading(s): tamilselvi, n. a., & pugalendhi, l. title: New Variety of ground nut-Moralo

details.full_description: genesis:   in the drought of 1987 and 1988, thakarshibhai purchased tagavi, saankdi and punjab-1 varieties from junagadh district sangh. on set of rains , he sowed punjab-1 variety. in 1988, while weeding and interploughing , he and his son (nitin) noticed 2 plants that stood out from the rest. they were greener, their leaves were thicker, the branches were longer, they bears more flowers and number of pods in the plants was higher too. these plants were marked and stored as seeds. in 1989, he sowed these seeds seperately. he collected the seeds again from new batch and sowed them again in 1990. he laso found that this variety had a tendency to spread in width when it grows. the crop ripened in 9 days a month, before the regular variety. the groundnut crop that he harvested , somehow resembled a peacock in shape. hence he named it moralo. this variety was developed on 26, september, 1988.                                                                                 salient characteristics: flowering (20-22 days), maturity period (90 days), oil content (48-51 %), yield (12-24 mann/bigha), number of nuts per pod (minimum of 2 nuts), taste (sweet), distance between rows (28'')

details.full_description: the traditional knowledge holder has suggested treatment for dysentery. disease symptoms: blood and mucus in stool, weakness, frequent bowel movement, lethargy ingredients: 21 fresh buds of akwan ( calotropis procera (aiton) w.t.aiton), 1 fresh leaf of todi ( luffa acutangula (l.) roxb.) and 2.5 dry fruits of golki ( piper nigrum l . ) preparation: place the buds on the leaf and heat it. crush them along with seeds to prepare a paste dosage/application: feed 100 g paste along with water to the animal twice daily for 2 days. ingredients' availability: the plants are available in nearby places.

title: Herbal Treatment for Diarrhoea

details.full_description:
the traditional knowledge holder has suggested
  treatment for diarrhoea. disease symptoms: frequent loose and watery motion, weakness. ingredients: 1 fresh root of chidchidi ( achyranthes aspera l . ) and 2.5 dried fruits of golki ( piper nigrum l.). preparation: collect, wash, and crush both the plant parts with 200 ml of water to prepare a mixture. dosage/application: consume 1 cup of prepared mixture thrice daily for 3-5 days. ingredients' availability: the plants are available in nearby places. suggested reading(s): girach, r. d., aminuddin & khan, s. a. (1992). ethnomedicinal uses of achyranthes apera l. in orissa (india). international journal of pharmacognosy, 30 (2), 113-115. shamkuwar, p. b., shahi, s. r., & jadhav, s. t.
(2012). evaluation of antidiarrhoeal effect of black pepper ( piper nigrum l.). asian journal of plant science and research , 2 (1),
48-53.

title: Herbal Treatment for Filariasis

details.full_description:
the traditional knowledge holder has suggested
  treatment for filariasis. disease symptoms : swelling in the legs, fever, pain, swelling of lymph glands ingredients: 50 g dried seeds of rai ( brassica nigra (l.) w.d.j.koch) and 100 ml of mustard oil. preparation: crush and fry the seeds with oil to prepare a paste. dosage/application: apply the paste over the affected area once daily till relief. ingredients' availability: the plant is available in nearby places and mustard oil is available in the local market.

title: Herbal Treatment for Menorrhagia

details.full_description:
the traditional knowledge holder has suggested
  treatment for menorrhagia. disease symptoms: heavy menstrual bleeding, pain, weakness. ingredients: 50 g dried seeds of til ( sesamum indicum l . ). preparation: crush partially and soak the seeds overnight in water. filter it in the next morning to prepare an infusion. dosage/application: consume the prepared infusion once daily on an empty stomach for 8-10 days. precaution: avoid intake of meat and spicy food. ingredients' availability: the plant is available in nearby places. suggested reading(s): rajith, n. p., ambily, d. v., dan, v. m., devi, p. s., george, v., & pushpangadan, p. (2012). a survey on ethnomedicinal plants used for menstrual disorders in kerala. indian journal of traditional knowledge,11 (3), 453-460.

title: Herbal Remedy for Increasing Strength of Working Bullock

details.full_description: the traditional knowledge holder has suggested remedy for increasing strength of working bullock. ingredients: 200 g whole plant of fimbriata ( caralluma fimbriata wall .) and 100 g seeds of black gram ( vigna mungo (l.) hepper . ) . preparation: collect, and crush both the ingredients together to prepare a paste. dosage/application: feed 300 g paste to the cattle once daily. ingredients' availability: the plants are abundantly available in all seasons at nearby places.

title: Herbal Treatment for Cold
keywords: Pachygone ovata (Poir.) Miers ex Hook.f. & Thomson

details.full_description: the traditional knowledge holder has suggested treatment for cold. disease symptoms: fever, shivering, nasal discharge ingredients: 100 g whole plant of pachygone ( pachygone ovata (poir.) miers ex hook.f. & thomson) and 200 ml buttermilk. preparation: collect plant and pound it well. to this add buttermilk. dosage/application: feed 300 ml mixture to the affected animal once daily till cure. precaution: green fodder should not be given. ingredients' availability: the plant is abundantly available in all seasons at nearby places. buttermilk is available in the local market.

title: Herbal Treatment for Fever

details.full_description: the traditional knowledge holder has suggested treatment for fever. disease symptoms: fever, shivering, nasal discharge, restlessness ingredients: 100 g leaves of kurchi ( holarrhena pubescens wall. ex g.don) and 100 g jaggery. preparation: collect both the ingredients. pound them well and dilute in 200 ml of water to obtain a mixture. dosage/application: feed 200 ml mixture to the affected animal once daily for 3 days. precaution: green fodder should not be given. ingredients' availability: the plant is abundantly available in all seasons at nearby places. jaggery is available in local market.

title: Herbal Treatment for Ectoparasites

details.full_description: the traditional knowledge holder has suggested treatment for ectoparasites. disease symptoms: itching, pus, weakness, hair loss, worms in wound ingredients: 100 g leaves of aloe vera ( aloe vera (l.) burm.f.) and 20 ml neem oil. preparation: cut the leaves and collect the gel. mix the gel with neem oil. dosage/application: apply the mixture to the affected area of the animal once daily for 5 days. ingredients' availability: the plant is available in nearby areas. neem oil is available in the local market.

title: Herbal Treatment for Leg Pain

details.full_description: the traditional knowledge holder has suggest ed treatment for leg pain ingredients: 10 g dry leaves of wild maracuja ( passiflora foetida l.). preparation: grind the leaves to make a fine powder and add 50 ml of water. dosage/application: feed 50 ml mixture to the animal once daily for 10 days. ingredients' availability: the plant is available in nearby areas.

title: Herbal Treatment for Leg pain

details.full_description: the traditional knowledge holder has suggested treatment for leg pain. ingredients: 10 g bark of pala indigo ( wrightia tinctoria (roxb.) r.br.) and 5 g jaggery. preparation: collect the bark and allowed to dry. crush it to make a fine powder. boil the powder into 200 ml of water and mix jaggery with it. dosage/application: feed 50 ml mixture to the affected animal once daily for 10 days. ingredients' availability: the plants are abundantly available in all seasons.

title: Herbal Treatment for Leg Pain

details.full_description: the traditional knowledge holder has suggested treatment for leg pain. ingredients: 10 g leaves of whitlow ( pergularia daemia (forssk.) chiova) and 10 g bulb of garlic ( allium sativum l.). preparation: collect and crush the plant parts together and add 200 ml of water. dosage/application: feed 200 ml mixture to the affected animal once daily for 10 days. ingredients' availability: the plants are available in nearby places.

title: Herbal Treatment for Fever

details.full_description: the traditional knowledge holder has suggested treatment for fever. disease symptoms: high body temperature, loss of appetite, drooling ingredients: 5 g dry leaves of whitlow ( pergularia daemia (forssk.) chiov.) and 2 g jaggery. preparation: grind both the ingredients to make a fine powder and add 200 ml of water. dosage/application: feed 200 ml mixture to the affected animal once daily for 10 days. ingredients' availability: the plant is available in nearby places. jaggery is available in the local market.

profile innovator mr. vijay kumar sendha hails from the bhadrak district of orissa. purpose mr. sendha has developed a wooden plough for seed bed preparation before sowing. technical details it is a single bottom country plough. the basic components of the plough are a shoe, share, body, handle, beam. when this plough is used in dry lands then shoes are generally of triangular section while in wet land cultivation the shoes are of a more flat section. performance innovator has claimed that the average depth of ploughing is 15 cm. benefits it is cheap, affordable and cost effective. suggested

title: Lathe machine running on break/ handle

details.full_description: purpose: in the village area, people used to face problems due to electricity cuts. machines like lathe, grinder, welding machine, etc. could not be operated and this hampered the work. to overcome the problem, mr. balwinder singh did some modifications to the pre-existing lathe machinery. technical specification: the headstock has been connected to a manual lever/ handle through an ms rod linkage so that the lathe spindle could be manually driven. this is a simple and effective method to work in the absence of electricity and long job works can also be handled. the innovator is using this technique for the past 25 years.

title: Dry Areca Nut Peeling Machine

details.full_description:
profile innovator mr. nithin n. prakash herale was born and
grown up in gajanur village of shimoga district in karnataka. his father shri prakash is a
farmer and mother smt. kamala is a homemaker. his younger sister ms. sanjana is
pursuing her engineering. his family owns agricultural land of 2.17 acres and
cultivate paddy, areca nut, coconut, rear cattle and have four cows. his day
starts with milking cows and helping his dad at fields. due to the family’s poor
financial condition, he had to discontinue his education and had to stay in sri
ramachandrapura mutt for two years. he is a serial innovator and has devised
need-based products to help farmer's community. purpose the peeling of areca nut involves highly skilled labor (generally ladies) using hand to peel areca nut. during the de-husking of dry areca, it is not only hard but also the dust and fine particles come out during peeling which is very harmful and it often leads to cases of asthma. during peeling, sometimes the finger also get cut during the operation. therefore, to reduce drudgery and other overlapping problems, the innovator developed a dry areca nut peeling machine. it is necessary to develop an arecanut peeling machine to increase the production rate and to decrease the consumption of time. this innovation is aimed at producing an efficient and more economical machine for areca nut peeling. technical details in the machine, areca nut is loaded into the hopper and the nut is one by one fed into a threshing drum. the drum has a rubber mold which tends to compress the nut and conveys it to a gear mechanism where the areca nut is peeled. the dust and fine particles are collected through a vacuum chamber which sucks them out of the system. performance the innovator has claimed that the machine has an output of up to 35 kg of clean areca nut per hour. benefits this machine is easy to use and shows an effective performance. suggested

title: Bicycle Weeder

details.full_description:
profile innovator mr. yogi lal singh is a farmer hailing from araria district of bihar. but he had and has no oxen for ploughing the field. he used to take oxen on rent for the purpose which added extra cost to his farming inputs. when his younger brother was about to sell his old cycle, he asked him not to sell it and decided to make some productive use of it. purpose mr. singh successfully developed a bicycle weeder out of the cycle. technical details for the construction of this weeder, he used the front part of the bicycle (wheel & handle). the rest of the cycle parts (rear wheel, seat, crank, chain, pedals, etc.) are removed. an iron rod is attached to the cycle behind the front tyre. a curved iron plate to serve as the plough tyne is attached to this rod, perpendicular to the ground surface. to operate this weeder, it is manually pushed against the ground surface. benefits it is simple in design, easy to make and low-cost weeder. suggested

title: Reaper

details.full_description:
profile innovator mr. hemshankar chaudhary hails from chhattisgarh. he is a farmer and a mechanic. purpose he had purchased a reaper from the market for rice harvesting but there were difficulties in harvesting operation using that reaper as he could not observe the cutting operation while driving. secondly, it was difficult to cross from one land to another with the reaper still attached to the tractor. therefore, he thought of making a new reaper that was void of existing problems. it is a tractor rear-mounted implement which receives drive through the pto shaft. performance the innovator has claimed that it has a width of cut of 200 cm and the height of cut is 5-7 cm. operated at a reverse speed of 12 km/h, it consumes about 2.5 l of diesel to cover 1 acre of land. also it can cover 1 acre of land in an hour. benefits the machine is suitable for the harvesting of rice, wheat and mustard plant. suggested

title: Leveler cum Loader

details.full_description: profile mr. hemshankar chaudhary hails from chhattisgarh. purpose labour shortage and demand from farmer friends, made the innovator think of a device that could be used for soil levelling and collecting. technical details initially, he had prepared the sketch design for leveller only but then modified it to carry the sand and help in shifting. this loader has a capacity of 300 kg and it can cover 1.5 acres per hour. it consumes about 2 l of diesel to cover 1 acre of land. overall, the implement is 6 ft in length, 2ft in height and weighs around 100 kg. benefits the implement can be used for agricultural and construction purposes and is most suitable for sandy soil. suggested reading(s): ministry of agriculture and farmers welfare, government of india, (2020). hand leveller. retrieved on january 7, 2021, from https://farmer.gov.in/dacdivision/machinery1/chap3b.pdf temesgen, m. title: Fertilizer Drill for Sugarcane Crop

details.full_description:
profile innovator mr. roshanlal vishwakarma hails from narsimhapur district of madhya pradesh. he has studied up to 11th standard. a skilled fabricator cum farmer par excellence, roshanlal has developed many agricultural and general utility machines. he also repairs farm implements and equipment and develops innovative machines at his workshop in his house. purpose in sugarcane cultivation, the sowing is done once in three years and for three years, sugarcane production can be achieved. but this requires regular application of fertilizer. the broadcasting technique of fertilizer application is not a very efficient technique as the fertilizer does not penetrate and reach up to the plant roots. moreover, a commercial machine is not available for natural manure/ worm manure applications in the field which could apply the manure directly in the roots of the plant. so, mr. roshanlal has made a machine that could be used to apply artificial fertilizer/ natural manure/ mixture of both in the sugarcane field. technical details the application is done on both sides of the plant. it is a tractor operated the machine and can be operated with any tractor of 25 hp and above. above the frame, a hopper, of 70 kg capacity, is mounted in which the fertilizer is filled. a spiral screw shaft is given for the proper mixing of the manure. this machine consists of cultivator tines mounted on a rectangular frame. performance the innovator has claimed that one acre area can be covered in one hour with this machine. benefits in this two-row cultivator, the manure is dropped in near the first-row tynes and the soil is covered up by the second row of tynes. suggested

title: Fodder Cutting Cum Mixing Machine

details.full_description:
profile innovator mr. roshanlal vishwakarma hails from narsimhapur district of madhya pradesh. he has studied up to 11th standard. a skilled fabricator cum farmer par excellence, roshanlal has developed many agricultural and general utility machines. he also repairs farm implements and equipment and develops innovative machines at his workshop in his house. purpose this innovation is to provide a proper nutritive mix of dry and green fodder, water and wheat flour to the milch animals. if nutritive food is not available to animals on time and that too in proper mixing proportion, the milk production is severely affected. the shortage of labor and the amount of labor involved in the task is huge and it is very difficult for one or two-man to mix fodder, chaff, etc. for as many as 15 animals and then feed them. therefore, to help himself and all people of his kind, mr. roshanlal developed a machine that could be used for fodder chopping and mixing with adequate and appropriate proportions of water, wheat flour, and fodder for feeding to animals. technical details the machine has separate feeding units (hoppers) for water, wheat flour, dry fodder and green fodder, which is manually fed into the horizontal feeding chamber, wherein it is chopped and then mixed with the other ingredients. the fodder, floor, and water is conveyed into the mixing chamber using different mechanisms such as screw conveyor, where they are received by the chopped green fodder. the mixture is then obtained from a vertically downward sliding output into a container. the complete machine runs with the help of a half hp single phase motor. benefits as such only one man is needed to operate the machine, feed the ingredients into the hoppers and feed the green fodder manually. the prepared mixture can then be given to animals. suggested reading(s): balami,

title: The improved public distribution system

details.full_description: profile innovator mr. roshanlal  vishwakarma hails from narsimhapur district of madhya pradesh. he studied up to 11th standard. a skilled fabricator cum farmer par excellence, roshanlal has developed many agricultural and general utility machines. he also repairs farm implements and equipment and develops innovative machines at his workshop in his house. purpose- usually, it has been found that in rural areas, the grains for pubic distribution by the fair price shops are kept open over the ground where they are exposed to the agents of weather, rodents, dust, dirt, etc. leading to their adulteration. therefore, to avoid the same and provide public with clean and fresh grains the innovator has suggested a method/ system of grain distribution in which an instrument/ machine is constructed having 3-4 containers having size as per the requirement so as to fill these containers with the grain. these containers are to be fitted with a lever at the outlet from where the grain can be dispersed. an electronic weight machine has to be placed below the outlet and a container has to be placed above that so that fair and equal quantity of grain can be distributed without possibilities of grain damage and rotting.

title: Multipurpose Seed Dibbler

details.full_description:
profile innovator mr. roshanlal vishwakarma hails from narsimhapur district of madhya pradesh. he has studied up to 11th standard. a skilled fabricator cum farmer par excellence, roshanlal has developed many agricultural and general utility machines. he also repairs farm implements and equipment and develops innovative machines at his workshop in his house. purpose traditionally seed sowing has been done by farmers manually or with the help of traditional seed dibbler where more labor is required. distance from one seed to another seed and depth of seeds can't be controlled properly. sometimes more seeds are dispersed. so, in the traditional method there is wastage of labor and seed. the innovator, therefore, developed a new type of seed dibbler for proper metering of seed. technical details the multi-crop seed dibbler is based on disc type seed metering mechanism. a rotating disk is fitted underneath the seed hopper and the seed is dispersed through the hole in the disk. the disc rotates as per the rotation of the ground wheel, therefore, maintaining the plant to plant distance. benefits this device is very cheap and affordable. using this seed dibbler, seeds of arhar (toor), corn, soybean, etc. can be easily sown. suggested

title: Seed Dibbler

details.full_description:

title: Sugarcane Bagasse Dryer

details.full_description:
profile innovator mr. roshanlal vishwakarma hails from narsimhapur district of madhya pradesh. he has studied up to 11th standard. a skilled fabricator cum farmer par excellence, roshanlal has developed many agricultural and general utility machines. he also repairs farm implements and equipment and develops innovative machines at his workshop in his house. purpose dry bagasse is used as a fuel in the jaggery manufacturing process. if the supply of bagasse is not continuously available, then this could hamper the production of jaggery. thus to quickly dry the bagassse (from which the juice has already been extracted), the innovator has suggested a sugarcane bagasse dryer machine. technical details this system of bagasse drying increases the overall system efficiency as the heat which is used for jaggery production is simultaneously used for bagasse drying. the system consists of a hollow metal pipe of cross sectional diameter equal to 12 inches. the pipe is cross sectionally cut to three fourth of the cross sectional area. a rectangular plate is mounted over this pipe along the length and a screw conveyor is fitted inside the hollow pipe. at the one end of the pipe, a hopper is mounted containing moist bagasse. the fire which is used for heating in jaggery production is lighted above this rectangular plate so that a part of heat is also used for drying of bagasse. as the bagasse is conveyed through the heated screw conveyor system, it dries. the dried bagasse is collected at the other end by a belt conveyor from where it can be directly used for burning purpose as a fuel. suggested reading(s): corrêa,

title: Insect Trapper in Ponds to Protect Fish Trapping

details.full_description:
profile innovator mr. jitendra das hails from the west midnapore district of west bengal. purpose breeding of insects in ponds is harmful to fish farming. therefore, to trap these insects, the innovator came up with the idea of an insect trapper in ponds. in earlier days most of his fish lings use to die because of insects. so, he has developed a low-cost method to save the fishlings from the harmful insect. technical details the system consists of a cylindrical container that is placed half-submerged inside the pond. an electricity bulb is mounted above the container using some bamboo splints or some other suitable method. the bulb can be powered using a battery or direct electricity. the container is filled with a mixture of water and pesticide. as the insects are attracted to the light, they fall in the container and thus die. in four corners of the pond, four wooden pillars are made where depth of water is 4 feet and with the help of
the wooden pillars a hollow cylindrical ring is made that is suspended
in such a way that 3 inch of the ring is submerged under water and 3 inches are above
the water. the diameter of the ring is 3 feet. a 5 watt bulb is placed
1 feet above the ring. parts used a ring made of 22 gedge g.i. sheet which is
12 feet long six feet long bamboo as a pillar for one ring 5 watt bulb 150-200 ml neem oil one 4 feet long g.i. wire in the evening the insect will be attracted to the light
bulb at this time if kerosene is poured inside the ring. the insect will fall
on the neem oil and will die. the insect which lives inside the water will be also
attracted to the light and when they will try to come in the upper surface of the water to reach the source of light it will die eventually because of the neem
oil. because of the metal ring, the neem oil will not be mixed up with the rest of the pond water and the next morning, the neem oil can be cleaned with a piece of

title: Three Layer Durable Water Pond

details.full_description:
profile the innovator is from idukki district of kerala. purpose these days there is a shortage of groundwater. the shortage of water can be overcome by utilizing the rainwater inefficient manner. for this purpose, the innovator created a three-layer durable water pond. technical details the dimensions of the pond depending on the geographical location of the plot and water source. the method of construction of pond includes the following steps - making a big right shaped pit by digging the land, then forming available crunch. after that first layer is made of an hdpe sheet. the pit is carefully covered with one layer of uv sterilized sheets. the final layer is 90% shade net. the bottom of the pond is filled with clean sand for about 1.5cm thickness. the borders of the pond thus made are covered with soil and mud and the suitable type of grass is grown on that. if the pond is for storing water for human consumption, it will be covered with a frame and plastic sheet to keep the water safe from sunlight.  if the pond is for fish farming, the bottom surface must be covered with good quality soil to assist the growth of microorganisms. also, a suitable quantity of cow-dung is mixed with the water in the pond to facilitate the growth of microflora and fauna which becomes the necessary fish food. benefits using this three-layered pond water can be efficiently conserved. suggested reading(s): deal, c. title: Electricity generation through from sea waves

details.full_description: profile mr. satvir gulia is a shopkeeper based in a small village badli of jhajjar district of haryana. purpose out of his many designs, this one is related to the generation of electricity through sea waves. mr. gulia applied for a patent for this one in the year 2005. technical details the said invention consists of lightweight & closed float which bounces in the sea because of the unstable and irregular motion of sea waves that operates the valves into a cylinder. the movement of float causes the piston of a small cylinder to operate. the created suction causes the valve to open. the opening of the valve pushes oil from the tank into a ram cylinder. as the oil gets stocked pistons of the ram cylinder start to lift under oil pressure and thus potential energy is generated. when the gate valve is opened manually, the oil turns a turbine at a constant rpm to generate electricity at a constant voltage. after moving the turbine, the oil returns back to the tank. benefit using this invention electricity can be generated from sea waves. this invention is eco-friendly. suggested reading(s): antonio, f. d. o. title: Modified hydraulic system for tractor

details.full_description: profile sh. mahavir singh, mr. mahavir singh is from the bhiwani district of haryana. he is a tractor mechanic, made a small device that can be fitted in the tractors in between the hydraulic pump and its drive gear. he has more than 33 years of experience in the workshop as a mechanic. purpose the fields in which farmers work are located at far locations, away from a mechanic shop. at times when there is leakage in hydraulic oil line of the lift system of the tractor, farmers have to tow back the engine to repair shop because when the engine of the tractor is switched on, the hydraulic system of the tractor is also switched on and there is oil continuously running through the hydraulic lines of the tractor. as they cannot drive it back, there is considerable loss of time, and work is hampered. to overcome the trouble of the farmers, sh. mahavir singh, who is a tractor mechanic, made a small device that can be fitted in the tractors in between the hydraulic pump and its drive gear. as such, using this device the hydraulic pump of the tractor can be disconnected even when the tractor engine is still on. thus, the farmers do not have to carry the tractor back by towing. technical details the components used for this hydraulic system of tractors are two bearings, two valves, valves bush, forges, oil plugs, forges nut, coupling. the forges are connected to the lever and these forges are connected to two bearings so friction loss is reduced and one part of forges are connected to two balls, these balls are touched to the shaft, the coupling is used to coupled the shaft and driving unit. the oil plugs used to fill oil in unit, the forges nut are used to tight the forges assembly. the power comes to engine and this device is used to stop the power when it is not used to the hydraulic system, the lever moves up and down that moves both balls also with forges. when the balls are backside than it is free to disconnect, while it comes again then it is connected to coupling and move with the engine. the oil pump operates the hydraulic system. benefit in driving the hydraulic pump of the tractor, up to 1 hp of power is wasted which can be thus saved. it also increases the life of the tractor pump, hydraulic oil, and improves the tractor engine performance. easy to use, easy to connect or disconnect the system in driving the hydraulic pump of the tractor, up to 1 hp of power is wasted which can be thus saved. it also increases the life of the tractor pump, hydraulic oil, and improves the tractor engine performance. title: Light Trap in Rice Field

profile mr. krishnapadda mallick lives in a small village, andharmanik in west bengal. he owns 1-acre field where he grows paddy, vegetable, etc. purpose he observed that when they light a fire during festivities, insects are attracted to it. inspired by this nature of things, he developed a frugal system to trap and kill insects in the field, at night. technical details at first, he experimented with a rag, dipped in mobil oil, burning to attract insects. it proved costly so he decided to use light bulb/ led lights. but for this purpose, he took a small open-ended bamboo stick. in this stick, he fitted a small torch with batteries and mounted it on a tripod made of sticks. underneath the tripod, a pan is put which contains a mixture of kerosene and water. the attracted insects fall into the pan and die. benefits this is a very cheap technique and can be used by anybody. it is known to farmers and many of them use very high wattage bulbs to attract insects. suggested

title: The art of Tabla making

details.full_description: profile: the innovator is a practitioner of the art of tabla making. he has been doing it since the age of 12 years. he introduced ring moot in tabala making. technical specifications: for making tabla, he uses goat and buffalo skin. the skin is cleaned with limestone and is dried after fixing in a wooden panel with the help of nails. the art of making tabla demands, the dried skin to be soaked in water prior using to making tabalas. for making murdungam, the wood of jackfruit tree is sued. the skin of goat is used for making the upper portion of the tabala and the thick thread is made from the buffalo skin. the black ink applied on the top is made up of poorna kiridam (mixture of iron and kary) and rice. after applying this on the tabala top, it is polished with krishna stone.

title: Iron Mesh Making Machine

details.full_description:
profile innovator mr. n. indrakumar singh hails  from thoubal district of	manipur. purpose mr. singh has developed the iron wire mesh making machine. technical details 18 pieces of an iron wire mesh having sizes of 23" x 23" is made from a full length of 45 feet iron wires in one shift. the square mesh sizes are varied from 5-10 mm length as per requirements. the present innovation is a simple treadle loom machine to make an iron mesh. it is quite similar to any other normal treadle loom, except that the new loom has four wheels and moves along as one weaves along. the machine looks like any other loom machine. it has a wooden frame, which is about 3-4 feet high and has 4 wheels on each of the legs. the wheels allow the machine to move forward or backwards.  it has two harnesses/shafts with heddles, and each harness has a set of heddles through which the warp threads (iron wire) are threaded. the recycled wires, removed from used tyres, are used as warp threads. since making a roll of wires is difficult, as in the case of other normal looms, a 30-40 feet long warp threads tied in two opposite frames at a given height (based on the height of a loom). the weft is also made recycled wires of the same kind. depending on the size of the mesh one wants to make, wires are cut into uniform lengths. the shafts are controlled by two pedals (treadles). the treadles keep the weaver's hands-free to manipulate the weft wire and it is easy to raise and lower warp threads. no shuttle is used in weaving; instead of cut iron wire (weft) is passed through in between the raised and lowered warp every time warp threads cross one another because of the treadle. the wrap threads also pass through a 'comb' attached to a slidable woven, the loom moves back towards the unwoven end. the gap between warp threads will vary for different types of fish (small or big)- normally it is about a cm or little less. the heddles are made of used cycle chains and iron wire. the 'comb' is also made of iron wires (nails) fixed on a wooden frame in equal distance. once the weaving is done, the woven iron mesh is cut into squares using a simple cutting knife. the open-ended sharp wires are rolled, using extra wires, into a round frill. recycle wire since buying of high tempered wire is quite expensive, the innovator has come up with an indigenous way of extracting the wire from used tyres. the rim of a tyre has a long coil of high tempered wire inside. the method of extraction is very simple- simply burn the tyres. it is not an environmentally friendly means of extraction; however, it is the simplest and least expensive means. benefits it is the only machine available for making an iron mesh. the treadle loom with wooden wheels allows the loom to move back and forth. it is a very low cost, doesn't need an expert hand to operate. it is an excellent way of recycling used tyres. it can give employment opportunities to the local people. the major applications of the iron wire mesh are for drying & smoking of fishes & meats, drying of vegetables. the other applications are for filtering sands and concrete for building constructions. suggested

title: Shock Proof Transformer

details.full_description:
profile innovator ms.sushila devi & mr.sanjay kumar lives in sik village, district panipat, haryana. both are uneducated and lives in poor economical condition. since childhood, both are very innovative & creative. purpose they always try to find a solution to an existing problem. especially problems related to electricity. they always hear about deaths because of electric shock. it distracts them so they came up with an idea and solutions that almost decrease the problem by 80-90%. technical details they design the shockproof transformer with it is primary & secondary both have three terminals. this transform neither step-up nor step down voltage/current nor drop its magnitude. it only provides better isolation and safety. benefits it is very very useful in household appliances, industries, and electricity distribution boards. suggested reading(s): del vecchio, r. m., poulin, b., feghali, p.

title: Combine Harvester

details.full_description:
profile innovator mr aagyaram verma is a farmer and an enterprising innovator from uttar pradesh who has studied up to 12th standard. purpose in order to harvest and store the wheat and paddy crops, a harvester was required which is small in size and which can travel in narrow lanes on the way to farms. technical details the combine harvester works with the help of a pto driven tractor (more than 35 hp - 40 hp). the cutter is assembled at the front of the tractor and the grain collector unit is assembled at the backside of the tractor. a trolly type system is attached to the tractor for collecting the husk which comes from the thresher unit. the length of the cutter is approximately 9 feet. the rotating wheel, 'reel' pushes the crops down towards the cutter. the cutter bar runs through the entire length of the header underneath the reel. the threshing drum beats and cuts crop to break and shake the grain away from other stalks. the grains fall through sieves into a collecting tank. the straw/ husk from the thresher is collected into a small trolly type attachment. the capacity of storing tank id 5 quintals. benefits this machine can harvest 1 acre of wheat in 2 hours by using 7 liters of diesel. performance of the machine is 1.5 hr per acre. the cost of a machine is approx. 4 to 5 lakhs. suggested reading(s): amponsah, s. k., addo, a., dzisi, k. a.,

title: Rice Milling Machine
keywords: rice milling machine with propeller shaft
belt pulley operated rice processing machine

details.full_description:
profile innovator mr. pussang is the second son of lt. mihin chaoyang
and smti. mihin sai in a small village tajang of arunachal pradesh. since
childhood, he was very curious about new things, but he was an average
student. he passed his middle standard from govt. middle school tajang and read
up to govt. hr. sec. school ziro. though he was curious about new things, he could
not do any remarkable invention and innovation due to a lack of resources and
proper education.  most of the time, he
indulged to earn a square of meals a day for his family. operation of rice
milling machine (rice huller) is one of his activity, now he runs a small scale fabrication work at old
ziro named as m/s nobin steel fabrication: ziro genesis of innovation / problem solved when pussang was operating a rice milling machine in his village, he
found that the belt runs out of the pulleys very often which interrupts the
smooth running of the rice milling machine. whenever he consults the problem
with a mechanic, they whimsically asked him for regular maintenance of the
machine and belts. pussang was not satisfied with their suggestion and was
looking for a permanent solution. as a result, an idea of fitting a propeller
shaft in place of a belt flashed in his mind and he tried with a jeep propeller
shaft. purpose rice milling involves the removal or separation of husk and bran to obtain the edible portion for consumption. pussang has made a modified coupling based rice huller. technical details construction this machine operated by
electrically powered having a rotary unit for mini rice mill mainly used for
dehusking/milling of straw. the main components of a mini rice mill are propeller
shaft, huller, cleaner, separator, hear plate, and feed hopper, conveyor screw. the major portion of the paddy is processed through
hullers but having a low capacity and result in some percentage of broken rice. working the principle of operation of mini
rice mill is that when power supply by the chain as well as gear drive to the
conventional paddy dehusking mechanism, then the huller shaft revolves in a particular direction says clockwise or anticlockwise direction. the shearing
force between the huller shaft and the fixed plate is responsible for rice milling the propeller shaft is a driving shaft which
connects the transmission main shaft to the differential of the rear axle. it
transmits the power from the gearbox to the rear axle with the help of universal
joints. the propeller shaft is also known as the driveshaft. it receives the power
from the gearbox output shaft and without any change in speed transmit it to
the input pinion of the differential for onward transmission to the rear axle
and rear wheels. to cope with the difference in line with the level of the gearbox output shaft and the differential input pinion shaft. performance a rice milling machine with a propeller shaft runs on its full capacity of
an engine, whereas a rice milling machine varied in capacity generation due to
adjustment of the belt. cost cost of rice milling machine with a propeller the shaft is rs. 2500/- benefits 1. it is a milling machine without a belt  propeller shaft is used to give motion, 2. it is used for small scale hulling process of rice. apart from rice it
can be used in other grains such as jobs tear, maize, etc. 3. this machine can be used for running a small scale
business so it may play an important social role. 4. both men and women can handle this simply constructed rice mill machine. suggested reading(s): afzalinia, s., shaker, m., & zare, e.
  (2004). comparison of different rice milling methods. canadian biosystems engineering , 46 (3), 63-66. dauda, s. m., adeoye, p. a., bello, k.,
  agboola, a. a., & abdulfatai, a. (2012). performance evaluation of a
  locally developed rice dehulling machine. international journal of agronomy and agricultural research , 2 , 15-21. dhankhar, p. (2014). rice milling. iosr journal of engineering, 4 (5), 34-42. goyal, s. k., jogdand, s. v., & agrawal,
  a. k. (2014). energy use pattern in rice milling industries—a critical
  appraisal. journal of food science and technology , 51 (11), 2907-2916.
